newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares sharply higher after CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares sharply higher after CPI.

text.p: Israeli shares closed sharply higher on increased turnover on Sunday after the release of a lower-than-expected January consumer price index (CPI), traders said.

"Investors were reacting to the lower-than-expected CPI and Wall Street's rise. Last week we saw a correction with falling volume, but now the market is recovering and turnover is rising," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 2.84 percent, or 7.18 points, to 259.87 on high all-share turnover of 188 million shekels against 123 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 3.07 percent higher at 266.97.

January CPI, released on Friday, rose 0.4 percent, compared with an 0.8 percent increase in December. The January index was slightly under estimates by government and private sector economists, who had forecast a rise of about 0.5 percent.

"The market was looking for a reason to rise and it came with the CPI figure. Despite that, we believe that inflation may accelerate in the coming months and that the central bank will not lower the rates," said Danni Scharia of Capital Securities.
"The main question is what will happen with interest rates. The Bank of Israel is not expected to reduce its key lending rate by more than 0.3 percentage points," Finn added.
Israel Discount Bank rose 3.0 percent to 374 agorot.

The government was due to offer shares and warrants equal to 17 percent of Discount's equity this week, but on Thursday the Securities Authority said it would not approve the prospectus unless it received more exact information on the bank's fourth-quarter doubtful-debt provision.
Officials involved in the planned offering in Israel on Sunday said they still hoped the offering could still go through.
"This is crazy it is not clear if the offering will go through but the share rises. The market is not acting in a rational way," said one trader.

The most active share was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which surged 5.5 percent to 19,528 agorot on volume of 11.3 million shekels; Israel Chemicals, which rose 4.5 percent to 379 agorot on turnover of 7.3 million shekels; and Leumi Insurance Holdings, which fell 1.0 percent to 249 on volume of 7.1 million shekels.
